subject: customize y-axis label of a density plot

messages.author: ba6f7beab14f01b8
messages.subject: customize y-axis label of a density plot
parts:
Dear List,

I would like to change the label for the y-axis of a density plot:

> qplot (rnorm(100), geom='density') + ylab ('Density')

however, the ylab() function doesn't seem to work here (nor does the
labs() variant) and the y-axis label remains the default 'density'.
Passing a ylab argument to qplot() doesn't seem to work either. I
copied details of my session below my signature. This is for a
publication and I would need the label to read 'Density' with capital
D.

Heartfelt thanks to Hadley for ggplot2, a truly wonderful package.

Any workaround / help highly appreciated,

Philippe

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: customize y-axis label of a density plot
parts:
Hi Philippe,

For this special case, you need to use the full form: +
scale_y_continuous("Density")

The reason is because the y axis is a computed variable, so at the
time you create the plot, ggplot doesn't know whether it will be a
continuous or discrete variable and so doesn't add a default scale
(like it does for all the other variables). xlab(), and labels() and
the xlab argument all working by modifying the existing scale, so they
don't work in this case because it doesn't exist.

Regards,

Hadley
